premises: F8 remains current repository claim authority for O5/D5 and has not been superseded by another repository claim epoch.
M56 binds I5 and I6 to sealed execution domain K5; P_I5 is complete only for K5 and its closed attempt set.
A later remap introduces I7, but M67_ambiguous does not establish whether I7 resolves to K5 or distinct domain K6.

fixture.candidate_action: Retain F8 as current repository ownership/fence evidence, but reject finalization based on P_I5 while I7's provider execution domain is ambiguous. Treat P_I5 as valid historical evidence for K5 only. Require either exact mapping resolution proving I7 remains in K5 or fresh terminal evidence covering the actual/all reachable I7 execution domains before any final repository CAS/readback. If repository authority changes while provider evidence is being repaired, reacquire the repository fence separately.
fixture.reason: Repository claim freshness and provider execution-domain coverage are independent safety dimensions. F8 proves current repository ownership, not that P_I5 covers a remapped identity whose execution domain may be K6. A fresh repository fence therefore cannot extend a provider proof beyond its exact domain scope.

weak_rule_falsified.rule: If repository claim authority is current, a previously valid provider terminal proof may be reused after an idempotency-identity remap even when the provider execution-domain mapping changed or became ambiguous.
weak_rule_falsified.falsification: F8 can remain perfectly current while I7 reaches K6, a domain not covered by P_I5. Finalizing from P_I5 in that state would convert a repository ownership fact into unsupported provider no-effect coverage and could miss an effect in K6.

fixture.minimum_safe_rule: A safe finalize requires both current repository claim authority and provider terminal evidence whose scope exactly covers the current idempotency identity's actual or conservatively reachable execution domain set. Freshness of one dimension never repairs staleness or ambiguity in the other; superseded proofs remain provenance only.

observations: The converse of c26 also fails: current repository authority does not rehabilitate provider evidence after provider execution-domain scope changes.
Identity remap ambiguity is itself sufficient to block no-effect finalization when the old proof is domain-scoped and a distinct uncovered domain remains reachable.
Repository claim/fence freshness and provider-domain proof coverage must be validated independently at finalize time.
inference: Within this exact deterministic fixture, safe cross-run idempotency recovery requires a two-dimensional freshness invariant: repository ownership must be current and provider evidence must exactly cover the currently reachable execution domain set. The invariant rejects both stale-repository/fresh-provider and fresh-repository/stale-provider asymmetries without requiring external arbitration.
